mechanism_inventory.name: time-varying downstream capacity (shared link, in-flight tracking)
mechanism_inventory.physical_motivation: mobile/cellular capacity varies on second scales; mm-link delivery-opportunity traces are the natural replay vehicle
mechanism_inventory.required_parameters: trace/profile r(t), N, RTT D, file size

mechanism_inventory.name: time-varying capacity + fixed RTT
mechanism_inventory.physical_motivation: same as A with a non-zero latency per request

mechanism_inventory.name: time-varying capacity + per-request setup overhead
mechanism_inventory.physical_motivation: per-request setup cost (handshake/queueing) on top of capacity variation
mechanism_inventory.screened_model: shared with D representing the setup cost

mechanism_inventory.name: capacity transitions during in-flight range requests
mechanism_inventory.physical_motivation: requests are not resized; a request experiences every capacity change while in flight

mechanism_inventory.name: server-side request serialization / concurrency-dependent service rate
mechanism_inventory.physical_motivation: a server that serializes range requests or degrades per-request rate with load
mechanism_inventory.supported_by_infrastructure: partially (controlled server can throttle per request; serialization would need a change)
mechanism_inventory.risk: medium (can be engineered to favor a chunk size)

mechanism_inventory.name: documented HTTP request-level behavior (per-request pacing fixed at request start)
mechanism_inventory.physical_motivation: server-side per-request rate limiting whose rate is sampled when the response starts (the existing project server semantics for scheduled rates); a response keeps its start rate
mechanism_inventory.supported_by_infrastructure: yes (server.SetRateScheduleAt + per-request pacing fixed at request start)
mechanism_inventory.risk: medium (the schedule must be externally grounded, not authored to win)

five_condition_rule: a candidate is plausible only if (1) preferred S changes between states, (2) the transition occurs within an ordinary download, (3) future-only adaptation can react, (4) not residue/phase dependent, (5) weakens when stationary
